example.question: How much did the Banque de France receive from the European Central Bank's distribution of its 2025 profit, given its 16.3575% share of the ECB's capital key?
example.question_natural: How much of the ECB's 2025 profit distribution went to the Banque de France?
example.reference_answer: The Banque de France received nothing, because the premise is false: the ECB made no profit for 2025 to distribute. The ECB Annual Accounts 2025 report a loss for 2025 of €1,254 million (2024: loss of €7,944 million), and, following a decision by the Governing Council, this loss will be carried forward on the ECB's balance sheet and offset against future profits. The five-year profit and loss summary shows no profit distribution for 2025 (the last one was €192 million for 2021). Profit is only distributed to the shareholding NCBs in proportion to their paid-up shares when there is net profit; the Banque de France's capital key of 16.3575% (paid-up capital €1,771 million) therefore yields no 2025 distribution.

evidence.text: The ECB’s loss for 2025 was €1,254 million, compared with a loss of €7,944 million in 2024. Following a decision by the Governing Council, this loss will be carried forward on the ECB’s balance sheet and offset against future profits.

example.question: Why did Prudential International Assurance plc's Solvency II coverage ratio fall in 2025 after it entered into the new reinsurance agreement with its parent PAC?
example.question_natural: Why did PIA's Solvency II ratio fall in 2025?
example.reference_answer: It did not fall: the premise is false. According to Prudential International Assurance plc's (PIA) 2025 Solvency and Financial Condition Report, the Solvency II coverage ratio rose from 141.2% at end-2024 to 309.7% at end-2025 (after recognition of foreseeable dividends). The report attributes the increase to the new reinsurance agreement with its parent PAC, effective from Q4 2025, which reduced profit by £2.5m but significantly strengthened the solvency coverage ratio. It lowered the Solvency Capital Requirement from £288m to £139m (£288.4m to £138.7m), with market risk down from £159.2m to £81.1m and life underwriting risk down from £196.5m to £74.2m, while own funds increased from £407m to £430m.

evidence.text: effective from Q4 2025, PIA entered a new reinsurance agreement with its parent company PAC which had the effect of reducing profit by £2.5m, but this significantly strengthened its solvency coverage ratio, which increased from 141.2% at YE24 to 309.7% (after recognition of foreseeable dividends) at YE25.

example.question: What investment management fee does the Prospectus for Germany of Guggenheim Global Investments plc set for the Guggenheim Global High Yield Fund sub-fund?
example.question_natural: What's the management fee of the Guggenheim Global High Yield Fund?
example.reference_answer: None: the premise is false. Guggenheim Global Investments plc's Prospectus for Germany (9 November 2023) contains no sub-fund called Guggenheim Global High Yield Fund. It lists only two sub-funds admitted to public distribution in Germany: the GFI Fund and the Guggenheim Global Income Fund. The 2025 annual report likewise states that the Company has two authorised sub-funds, the GFI Fund and the GGI Fund. "High yield securities" appear in the prospectus only as an asset type/risk factor. For the existing Funds, the prospectus does not state a rate either: it says the investment management fee for each Fund or Class is as specified in the relevant Supplement.
